subject: Renewal: smoothing uptake + auto-renew safeguard for Acme AI
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@acme.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + spike in usage next quarter

Hi Michael,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're preparing our FY plan and it looks like our usage of Redwood will ramp significantly in Q3 due to a larger feature rollout. Our renewals team asked me to coordinate early so we can lock in a structure that lets us scale without surprise overages.

High-level ask: can we discuss a 24-month renewal with an upfront commit that ramps across quarters, plus an auto-renew "safeguard" clause so we avoid service interruptions while procurement wraps up? Procurement asked for a simple canary/overage buffer for the first two quarters of the new term.

Attached is a CSV with our projected token burn and the Q1 usage as context (Q1-usage-breakdown.csv). Would love 30 minutes this week to align.

Thanks,
Sam
Director of AI Products
Acme AI

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@acme.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + spike in usage next quarter

Sam — thanks for the heads-up and the data. We can absolutely structure something that covers a quick ramp without leaving you exposed or locking you into unnecessary spend. Proposed approach (high-level):

- 24-month term, with quarterly committed token buckets that step up (Q1: 25% of annual, Q2: 35%, Q3-Q4: remaining)
- Upfront commitment equal to 50% of year 1 to reduce unit price; remainder invoiced quarterly
- 60-day canary/overage buffer: if committed usage is exceeded within first 60 days, we consume buffer credits first (at discounted rate) and then invoice true overage; buffer resets at start of Q2
- Auto-renew default opt-in with 90-day notice to opt-out; procurement can disable auto-renew via written notice to avoid surprises

Operational asks from our side:
- A signed term sheet and SOW with projected traffic windows to enable capacity planning
- An aligned contact in procurement and a legal point-of-contact for standard redlines

I attached a draft term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf) that captures the above and a sample ramp schedule. Vanessa — can you flag anything here that needs an escalation path or SLA credit language? Jordan — can you prep a DocuSign-ready version if the customer is happy so we can hit their requested timeline?

If that approach looks good, I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment on Thursday.

Best,
Michael
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sam Park <sam.park@acme.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + spike in usage next quarter

Thanks Michael — looks sensible. A couple of internal notes:

- SLA fallback: for the 60-day canary we should include a capacity-fallback clause that routes to an alternate region or model family if per-region allocation is exhausted; this avoids a hard outage for them.
- Credit mechanics: define the credit as a percentage of monthly committed fees prorated to the impacted window (we've used 10% for shortfalls historically).
- Finance: Jordan, confirm whether upfront 50% payment requires an invoice hold or if we can net against existing credits.
- Legal: if legal@acme.ai needs to redline, require a single consolidated redline within 7 business days to keep the timeline.

Sam — two quick questions for you before Thursday: who will be the legal POA to receive DocuSign, and does procurement need the auto-renew default turned off for enterprise policy reasons? If so we can change to an opt-in renewal with the same economics but require re-sign within the renewal window.

-Vanessa
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@acme.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acme.ai, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Finalized term sheet + next steps (DocuSign link)

Sam / procurement / legal — attaching finalized term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf) with the clarified SLA fallback and credit language Vanessa requested. Key changes in this version:

- Explicit fallback routing (regional failover) during canary window
- Credit calculation clause (10% cap for single event, prorated)
- Procurement requested: removal of auto-renew default; changed to auto-notify with 30-day re-sign window (we left an explicit opt-in path if they prefer auto-enroll economically)

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/link/abcdef123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2028-RNW-42

Attachments: redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf

Next steps for Acme:
1) Legal to send consolidated redlines within 7 business days
2) Procurement to confirm payment cadence (upfront 50% vs net-30)
3) We run a short capacity canary in week 1 of the new term to validate routing rules

Sam — please let us know the legal POA and whether procurement needs the auto-renew change. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan
Sr. Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference

---
